title: Timing oscilloscope - peak-stitch diary
content:
Notes-to-self: ran a small 'timing-oscilloscope' style probe to look for inter-region skew and composite peaks that show up only when stitching traces from multiple edge gateways. Goal: verify whether reported p95 spikes are real or an artifact of sampling alignment + clock skew.

Background:
- Production reports intermittent p95/p99 spikes (~200-400ms above baseline) at 03:xx UTC over the last 3 days. Spikes correlate with multi-region routing changes and light autoscaling.
- Hypothesis: independent small peaks in different regions, when merged after ingestion, produce an apparent higher quantile due to timestamp skew and sampling window boundaries.

Quick setup:
- Lightweight probe clients (k6-style) deployed to 3 regions: us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1.
- Request pattern: Poisson arrival lambda=35 RPS total (split evenly), payload small (prompt ~40 tokens).
- Run length: 30m warm, 60m steady, 15m cooldown.
- Sampling: both full-trace and 1-in-100 sampled traces. Also recorded local monotonic timestamps at the client and server-side receive timestamps.
- Clock sync: NTP drift observed up to 120ms on eu-west1 VM (ugh). Added monotonic delta adjustments post-facto.

Experiment configs tried (short names):
- A: aligned windows (fix window boundaries on gateway ingestion)
- B: naive merge (just concat traces by wallclock)
- C: stitched-with-skew-correction (apply local monotonic deltas then merge)
- D: high-res-sample (increased sampling to 1-in-10 during flagged spike windows)

Raw numbers (steady-state median baseline ~48ms):
| config | region | p50 | p95 | p99 | notes |
| A | us-west1 | 46ms | 72ms | 120ms | clean
| A | us-east1 | 49ms | 78ms | 137ms | clean
| A | eu-west1 | 51ms | 90ms | 220ms | occasional +clock-drift
| B (merged) | combined | 49ms | 140ms | 410ms | big uplift — suspicious
| C (corrected) | combined | 49ms | 85ms | 160ms | much closer to reality

ASCII oscilloscope (combined p95 over time / 1m buckets) — illustrative:
time  | p95 (ms)
00:00 | ████  72
00:01 | ████  68
00:02 | ██████████ 145  <-- merged peak in naive merge (B)
00:03 | ███  60
00:04 | █████  96
00:05 | ███████ 130
(peak stitching moments align with region handoffs and eu-west NTP jitter)

Observations / reasoning:
- Naive merge (B) doubles down on peaks: small +50ms peaks in different regions that do not overlap in wallclock time can, after ingestion buffering and windowing, fall into the same quantile bucket and create a composite outlier.
- Clock skew in eu-west1 (~80-120ms) explained a lot of the apparent >200ms p99 values. Once corrected (C), the combined p99 dropped by ~60% in these runs.
- Sampling resolution matters: 1-in-100 missed many short-duration microspikes; when we increased sampling (D) in flagged windows, we captured microbursts that accounted for ~20% of p99 mass.
- Edge routing flips (we simulate a region failover) cause transient queuing at proxies; those transient queues are real and contribute to observed spikes. Distinguish these (real queuing) from composed artifacts (stitching).

Immediate actionable items:
- Add monotonic-timestamp delta to ingestion pipeline so stitching uses corrected monotonic time by default (low-effort, high-impact).
- Increase high-res sampling when any region reports NTP drift >50ms or when autoscale events occur.
- Update SLO detection: use per-region quantiles + a stitched-but-corrected combined stream to trigger alerts. Avoid naive merged quantiles for alerting.

Questions / open points:
- How often do our customer-facing dashboards use naive merged quantiles today? Need inventory. (Maya to check dashboard configs).
- Is there any path-dependent bias when requests are retried or fall back to smaller model variants? Could create correlated peaks across regions.
- Need to decide whether ingest-time correction or post-facto analysis is the canonical source of truth. My leaning: fixed ingest-time monotonic delta simplifies downstream consumers.

To-do (short):
- [ ] Prototype ingest-time monotonic delta patch (small PR) — target: feature-branch by 2024-11-20.
- [x] Re-run with increased sampling windows (done 2024-11-18) — rough capture attached (see linked PR).
- [ ] Add dashboard panel showing "stitch-loss" (difference between naive merged p95 and corrected merged p95) per-1m bucket.

Notes to self: keep the oscilloscope metaphor — visualizing small time-lagged peaks helps convince folks this is not a single monstrous event. When we present, show side-by-side: naive-merge vs corrected-merge vs per-region.

Appendix - run checklist / env details:
- Client binary: bench-probe:v0.5.3
- Kernel: ubuntu-22.04, NTPd (yes), ntpstat reports drift pre-correction: us-west1 ~ 12ms, us-east1 ~ 8ms, eu-west1 ~ 94ms.
- Ingestion buffer: 200ms default, tried 50ms / 400ms variants. 200ms seems ok after correction.
- Logs: stored in gs://redwood-bench/oscilloscope/2024-11-12/ (raw traces + processed tables).

If I get time: run a longer 4-hour nightly run with simulated route-flip at t+90m to capture realistic failover pattern. Otherwise present these notes in the Friday sync with SRE and Product.

-- Ryoji
